content: 3-axis CNC g-code assumes a fixed tool orientation (Z always vertical) so X/Y/Z fully describe the toolpath; robot arms have 6+ DOF so the same nominal toolpath requires full pose (position + orientation, often as quaternion/Euler) at each point, and reaching that pose is an IK problem rather than a direct axis move. Robotic g-code post-processors/interpreters must therefore either (a) assume a fixed constant tool orientation, simplifying to CNC-like motion, or (b) carry orientation data per point (e.g. via extended/custom g-code fields, since standard g-code has no native multi-axis orientation syntax) and run IK per point. A parser that only reads X/Y/Z/I/J/K and ignores tool orientation will produce wrong robot poses for anything but simple 3-axis-equivalent operations.
